ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account is primarily budget-constrained across nearly all scalable campaigns: most sit at ~17–22% impression share while losing ~78–83% to budget and running at ~99.9% budget utilization, with essentially 0% lost to rank at the campaign level. Efficiency is mixed (Shopping ROAS ~1.4–2.0; Non-Brand Search ROAS 1.68), so the opportunity is to reallocate/increase budget into the highest-return slices while pruning waste (very low quality-score, high CPA keywords; competitor-brand zero-click leakage) rather than simply “spend more everywhere.”
notable_patterns: Five in-scope growth campaigns (Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo, Performance Max - Full Catalog, Shopping - Apparel/Electronics/Home & Garden) are all effectively capped (budget_utilization_pct 99.9%) while losing the majority of eligible exposure to budget (lost_budget_pct 79–83%) and showing low impression share (17–21%).

Brand Search - US is not rank-limited (lost_rank_pct 0%) and is not fully budget-capped (budget_utilization_pct 75.4%), but it still loses 40% impression share to budget with strong ROAS (10.51; $53,035.50 revenue on $5,047.88 spend), implying budget headroom exists within the account that could be shifted without harming efficiency.

Keyword evidence flags rank/bid pressure at the query level even where campaign-level rank loss is reported as 0%: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5) shows 19% IS with 81% lost to rank; “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0) shows 21% IS with 79% lost to rank—suggesting certain ad groups/keywords may still need bid/coverage tuning once budget caps are relieved.

Waste/leakage signals: competitor-brand zero-click terms generate 8,280 impressions and represent 51% of search-term impressions from zero-click competitor terms, while low-QS keywords consume spend with very poor cost per conversion (e.g., “deals near me today” QS 2.5; spend $152.52; cost/conv $762.6).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Impression share is only 18% while 82% is lost to budget and the campaign is fully capped (budget_utilization_pct 99.9%). With ROAS at 1.45 ($7,981.17 revenue on $5,491.96 spend), scaling without improving feed/product mix risks amplifying low-margin volume.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget only after tightening product segmentation and excluding/downsizing low-return inventory; then reallocate incremental budget to the best-performing product groups to capture the 82% lost to budget.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Severely supply-limited by budget (17% impression share; 83% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) but currently inefficient (ROAS 1.42; $5,046.45 revenue on $3,550.60 spend).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Do not broadly raise budget yet; first cut/segment weak electronics inventory and resolve any query-level rank/bid gaps on high-intent terms (e.g., ‘holiday electronics deals’ IS 19% with 81% lost to rank) before scaling.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Budget is the clear limiter (19% impression share; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) and ROAS is comparatively best among Shopping (1.88; $7,338.68 revenue on $3,896.20 spend), making it the strongest Shopping candidate for incremental budget.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Reallocate incremental budget into Home & Garden first (from lower-ROAS Shopping/Audience) to capture more of the 81% lost to budget while monitoring marginal ROAS.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Strong efficiency signals (avg quality score 8.8) but heavily throttled by budget (21% impression share; 79% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization). It also contains measurable internal blocking: 3 negative conflicts suppress ~6,940 impressions, including ‘free’ blocking 5,200 impressions.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Fix negative-keyword conflicts immediately and then fund controlled expansion; also remove/contain low-QS, high-CPA keywords dragging performance (e.g., QS 2.5–3.5 terms with $139–$763 cost/conv).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Meaningfully constrained by budget (19% impression share; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) with ROAS 2.15 ($2,132.20 revenue on $994.03 spend), suggesting incremental budget could scale profitably if search-term leakage is controlled.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget selectively after tightening query coverage (exclude/limit competitor-brand zero-click traffic where possible) and ensuring best-margin products receive priority.

recommendation_cards.title: Reallocate budget from low-return areas into capped, higher-ROAS campaigns (start with Brand + Home & Garden + Performance Max)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Most growth campaigns are hard-capped (budget_utilization_pct 99.9%) and losing 79–83% impression share to budget (e.g., Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo lost_budget_pct 79%; Shopping - Electronics 83%; Performance Max 81%). Meanwhile Brand Search - US is under-utilizing budget (75.4% utilization) but still shows strong ROAS 10.51 ($53,035.50 revenue on $5,047.88 spend), indicating room to fund more efficient demand capture. Within Shopping, Home & Garden has the strongest ROAS (1.88) vs Apparel (1.45) and Electronics (1.42).
recommended_steps: Reduce/hold budgets on the weakest-return campaigns first (e.g., Shopping - Electronics ROAS 1.42; Shopping - Apparel ROAS 1.45) and shift that daily budget into Shopping - Home & Garden (ROAS 1.88) and Performance Max (ROAS 2.15).

If total budget can increase, stage increases in 10–20% increments on the capped winners (Home & Garden, Performance Max, then Non-Brand Search after clean-up), rather than lifting all Shopping budgets evenly.
Keep Brand Search funded enough to reduce its 40% lost-to-budget while watching for diminishing returns (it’s currently only at 60% impression share).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Lost impression share to budget on the scaled campaigns dropping from ~81–83% toward <60% while holding marginal ROAS at or above current levels (Home & Garden ~1.88; Performance Max ~2.15).

recommendation_cards.title: Fix internal negative-keyword conflicts blocking your own promo queries (recover ~6,940 impressions)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 3 conflicts blocking an estimated 6,940 impressions in Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo. The biggest is negative “free” blocking the keyword “free shipping promo code” (estimated 5,200 blocked impressions). Additional blocks: negative “DIY” blocking “kitchen appliances clearance DIY install” (980) and negative “returns” blocking “winter jacket sale returns policy” (760).
recommended_steps: Move the conflicting negatives (“free”, “DIY”, “returns”) to a narrower scope (apply only where truly intended) or replace with more precise variants so they don’t block the listed keywords.

After resolving, re-check query matching to ensure the intended promo/seasonal queries can serve, but add tighter exclusions for clearly non-commercial ‘free’ intent if needed (see the low-QS cleanup card).
Monitor the previously blocked keywords/ad groups for traffic and conversion quality for 7–14 days before expanding budgets further.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impressions and conversions on the previously blocked keyword themes; target: recover a meaningful portion of the ~6,940 blocked impressions without worsening cost/conv in the campaign.

recommendation_cards.title: Cut or isolate low-quality, high-CPA keywords that are burning budget under the promo campaign
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several keywords show very low quality score with disproportionate cost per conversion: “deals near me today” (QS 2.5; spend $152.52; cost/conv $762.6), “kitchen appliances clearance” (QS 3.0; spend $97.52; cost/conv $325.07), and “free shipping promo code” (QS 3.5; spend $250.38; cost/conv $139.1). In a campaign already losing 79% of impressions to budget, this wasted spend directly reduces the ability to buy incremental high-intent volume.
recommended_steps: Pause or heavily down-bid the worst offenders first (“deals near me today”, “kitchen appliances clearance”) and move any remaining exploratory terms into a separate, tightly capped test ad group/campaign.
Add intent-shaping negatives for ‘near me’/local browsing and other low-commercial modifiers observed in poor-performing terms to prevent repeat spend.
Shift the freed budget into higher-intent seasonal terms/ad groups (where QS is already strong in this campaign: avg_quality_score 8.8).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Promo campaign cost per conversion improving materially (aim to beat the current worst pockets like $325–$763/conv) while maintaining or growing total conversions above 81.6.

recommendation_cards.title: Block/limit competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ leakage that is inflating impressions without returns
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand zero-click terms generated 8,280 impressions and account for 51% of search-term impressions from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “metro retail co”, “northfield mercantile”, “union square goods”). Only 0.2 conversions are attributed to a competitor-flavored term (“fairmont retail quote”), indicating minimal payoff relative to volume.
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names from the zero-click list as negatives in non-brand/search expansion areas where they don’t serve a deliberate conquesting strategy.
If conquesting is desired, isolate it into a dedicated campaign with capped budget and tailored messaging, instead of allowing it to leak into core efficiency campaigns.
Re-audit search terms after 7 days to confirm competitor impressions and spend drop while conversions hold.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms dropping from 51% toward <20% with stable overall conversion volume.

recommendation_cards.title: After budget caps are relieved, address query-level rank gaps on high-intent seasonal terms
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Despite campaign-level lost_rank_pct reported as 0%, keyword-level data shows significant rank loss on valuable seasonal queries: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5; impression share 19%; lost rank 81%) and “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0; impression share 21%; lost rank 79%). This suggests certain ad groups/keywords may be under-bid or constrained by coverage settings once additional budget is available.
recommended_steps: Once negative conflicts and low-QS waste are fixed, increase bids (or loosen constraints) specifically on the high-QS seasonal keywords showing 79–81% rank loss.
Confirm these terms route to the most relevant landing pages and product sets (electronics deals vs winter apparel) to preserve QS while scaling.
Use auction outcomes as guardrails (self top-of-page rate 49.6% vs competitors 42.4% on average) to avoid overbidding broadly; focus only where rank loss is documented.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share on the listed seasonal keywords rising from ~19–21% toward 30%+ while keeping cost/conv stable or improving.

already_working: Ad quality is not the bottleneck: 100% of ads are rated Good or Excellent (4 Excellent, 4 Good), so copy refresh is not an urgent lever right now.

At the account competitive level you are not being dominated in auctions: avg outranking share is 52.9% and your avg top-of-page rate (49.6%) is above the competitor average (42.4%), indicating the bigger limiter is budget allocation/caps rather than widespread rank collapse.

Brand Search is highly efficient (ROAS 10.51 on $5,047.88 spend with 536 conversions), so scaling brand coverage to reduce its 40% lost-to-budget is low risk compared with scaling low-ROAS Shopping broadly.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Retail search competition and spend are rising right now, while this account is only capturing ~17–22% impression share and losing ~78–83% of eligible impressions to budget. In a market where search represents a large share of category investment, staying budget-capped (and allowing waste/leakage) risks forfeiting near-term demand capture—especially around seasonal queries showing renewed growth (e.g., “winter jacket sale”). Acting now to reallocate budget into the highest-ROAS capped campaigns (and eliminate internal waste like zero-click competitor leakage and negative conflicts) is urgent because the external environment is expanding and competitors are actively investing in Search/Shopping.

supporting_facts.fact: Retail (United States) shows Search Spend Growth QoQ of 9.0% and Query Demand Growth QoQ of 6.0%, with Vertical-Avg Impression Share at 35.0%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: With the market’s search spend and demand both growing (9.0% and 6.0% QoQ), remaining capped at ~17–22% impression share means the account is under-participating versus the vertical norm (35.0%) precisely as demand expands. This supports urgency to relieve budget caps—selectively via reallocation to the best-return campaigns—so the account doesn’t fall further behind in share while the auction gets more expensive and active.

supporting_facts.fact: United States (pilot account market): Search Spend Growth QoQ is 9.0% and Vertical-Avg Impression Share is 35.0%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A rising spend environment (+9.0% QoQ) typically increases auction pressure; if the account continues losing ~78–83% of impressions to budget, it effectively opts out of incremental auctions. The 35.0% vertical-average impression share also reinforces that current ~17–22% share is materially below a common benchmark, strengthening the case to act now on budget reallocation and waste-pruning to capture more available inventory.

supporting_facts.fact: Search accounts for 30% of category spend.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Because Search represents 30% of category spend, Search is a core battleground for Retail demand capture. Being broadly budget-constrained on Search/Shopping while competitors invest means missed reach is strategically costly; it’s not a marginal channel. This supports urgency to fix budget allocation (fund capped winners; prune low-QS/high-CPA waste and competitor leakage) rather than waiting.

supporting_facts.fact: The keyword “winter jacket sale” index rises from 100 (Q4 2025) to 121 (Q3 2026), a Growth of 21%.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: The account already shows a query-level constraint on “winter jacket sale” (low impression share and high loss), and external data shows this query theme is growing (+21%). That combination increases urgency: if budgets and targeting/rank issues aren’t addressed now, the account is likely to miss a growing seasonal demand pocket.

supporting_facts.fact: Metro Retail Co has 28% Spend Share and is active on “Search, Social, Video”.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A competitor with a large spend share (28%) actively invests in Search, indicating meaningful competitive presence in auctions the account is currently unable to fully enter due to budget caps. This supports urgency to stop forfeiting impression share to budget—starting with the most efficient/capped campaigns—so competitors with high spend share don’t consolidate demand.

supporting_facts.fact: Northfield Mercantile has 21% Spend Share, 51 Active Creatives, and is active on “Search, Social”.
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: High spend share (21%) plus substantial creative activity (51) suggests sustained competitive marketing pressure that can raise CPCs and reduce available impression share. With the account already losing ~78–83% to budget, delaying budget reallocation and waste cleanup likely compounds missed reach as competitors continue pushing.

email_copy.subject: USD 54,575 in missed revenue while 78.7% of impressions are lost to budget
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t being out-ranked — it’s being throttled. Right now you’re capturing just 21.29% impression share while budgets are effectively maxed out across the campaigns that should be driving growth.
why_now_bullets: The market is getting more expensive/active: Search Spend Growth QoQ is 9.0%, and you’re currently opting out of a big chunk of auctions by losing 78.7% of eligible impressions to budget.
You’re under-participating versus the norm: vertical-average impression share is 35.0% while you’re at 21.29%.

Seasonal demand is ticking up where you’re constrained: “winter jacket sale” shows 21% growth (index 100 to 121), and your account data already shows that theme is being limited by coverage/rank once budgets loosen.
email_copy.impact_line: At a daily budget of USD 9,400, the bigger issue isn’t “spend more everywhere” — it’s that high-intent campaigns are capped while pockets of waste/leakage siphon off dollars that should be buying incremental demand. Clearing the internal blockers and shifting budget into the highest-return, currently-capped areas is what unlocks the USD 54,575.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is where that upside is concentrated by campaign, based on what’s currently capped vs. what’s actually returning value.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here are the specific moves that remove the throttle first (budget + internal waste), then add coverage only where the data shows it will hold efficiency.
email_copy.working_intro: A quick reassurance before the fixes: the foundation is solid — performance is being limited by allocation and caps, not a broken account.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: Once the waste is cut and the right campaigns are funded, the upside is straightforward: moving from 21.29% impression share toward 35.0% maps to an estimated 315330 additional impressions and 12320 additional clicks (using today’s 3.91% click rate as the conservative baseline).
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map the exact budget shifts + negatives in your account?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with either “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send two times. If easier, just reply “plan” and I’ll share the 1-page rollout order first.
email_copy.ps: PS — You’re showing 0.0% lost to rank at the campaign level, so this is a cleaner win than most: fix the self-inflicted blockers, then buy back the demand you’re currently missing due to budget caps.
